newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TAMPA BAY BEATS MONTREAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TAMPA BAY BEATS MONTREAL.

text.p: Mikael Andersson's shorthanded goal with two minutes left broke a tie and Chris Gratton had two goals as the Tampa Bay Lightning ran their unbeaten streak to five games with a 4-2 victory over the Montreal Canadiens on Monday.

John Cullen also scored and Rob Zamuner had two assists for the Ligntning, who are 4-0-1 in their last five games following a six-game losing streak. Rick Tabaracci made 22 saves for the victory and has allowed just nine goals in his last five games.

"The last two weeks have been great for us, it shows we're working," Tabaracci said. "We are playing hard and aggressive hockey, everyone is taking a part in our production and I think we've turned it around."
In New York, Wayne Gretzky had a goal and an assist and Mark Messier set up a goal in his return to the lineup, lifting the New York Rangers to a 5-2 victory over the Hartford Whalers.
The Rangers moved a game above .500 (15-14-5) for the first time this season, and got back Messier, who missed five straight games with an elbow injury.
"A couple of times I got in position when it twinged a little, but I felt pretty good and I was real happy not re-injuring it," Messier said.
Mike Richter made 39 saves for the Rangers.
"We got off to a slow start and they made the most of some chances," Hartford coach Paul Maurice said. "That certainly snowballed and it was too late by the time we began to right the ship.

At Calgary, Mike Dunham made 28 saves for his first career shutout and Brian Rolston scored twice in the first five minutes of the second period to lift the New Jersey Devils to a 5-0 victory over the Calgary Flames.
Dunham, in his 10th NHL game, made seven saves in the first period, 13 in the second and eight in the third as New Jersey improved to 3-0-1 in its last four games.
Dwayne Roloson made 25 saves for the Flames, who lost at home to New Jersey for the first time in five years.
